direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is very similar to other Dreamworks properties, but they do a good job building this world and showing the grand flying and fight scenes; The direction on a microscale is pretty good as it shows the internal struggle Hiccup has with his father and how he doesn't want to be a Viking or hurt others; The storytelling is pretty similar to other Dreamworks movies and pretty predictable given this is a PG movie

performance.comments: Feels a little too old playing this role, but does a pretty good job embodying the awkwardness and nerdy nature of Hiccup
Really embodies the character and the big stature the chief has over Berk and the disconnect he has with his son
He plays his role well and has pretty good chemistry with Baruchel
Plays the female lead decently well but does not really have the best chemistry with Baruchel

cast.comments: A pretty all-star cast, but it feels like they are just speaking and not really embodying the characters they are portraying

story.comments: The concept is a similar trope to the "Dances with Wolves" teen who learns to be with the opposition rather than fight them; though it does so in a way that is palatable for children and makes them care for the dragons and the characters; the plot structure is very linear and formulaic, especially for a DreamWorks property, because the movie is pretty short and the pacing is very fast; the character writing is good as they do paint Hiccup as this multi-dimensional character who has to go against what his father wants for him because of his morals, and they do a good job showing the growth in all the characters

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is good and memorable, especially for a PG movie; The humor is mostly attached to your caring about these characters; The symbolism is pretty strong as the movie touches on the tough father-son dynamic between two generations with different morals; The foreshadowing is strong as the movie plants roots that are uprooted towards the end

score.comments: Very memorable score that helps build the world and sets the tone

sound.comments: It helps with building this grand world

animation.comments: For the time, it was probably very good; but this style of CGI animation that DreamWorks was known for in the 2000s has not aged well at all, as the technology looks very out-of-date; something that was going to happen when studios favored technology-dependent 3D animation over timeless 2D animation

review.pacing: Pacing is incredibly fast as the movie breezes through the plot to get through its short runtime; Because of these pacing issues, many of the scenes and sequences don't feel like they have time to breathe
review.climax: Climax is executed well but feels very fast and short; Also, the final antagonist does not really make sense the more you think about it
review.tone: Tone is similar to other DreamWorks properties, mixed with Norse and dragon mythology
review.overall: Overall, a pretty good movie that lays the foundation for a memorable franchise and lovable characters like Hiccup, Toothless, and Stoick; but, it is held back by its incredibly fast pace and dated 3D animation
